title: Matter wave bistability with a momentum chirped Bose-Einstein condensate
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Nicholas Mantella, Noah P. Baker, Joseph McGowan, Aephraim M. Steinberg
abstract: While a Fabry-Perot (FP) cavity interferometer is a standard tool in modern optics, analogous physics can also be observed with matter waves such as Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs). Interatomic collisions in BECs can induce nonlinear features such as multi-valued transmission spectra for interferometry experiments. Observation of interaction effects in the matter-wave analogue of FP interferometry has not yet been experimentally achieved, mostly due to broadening of transmission peaks by interaction-induced shifts of cavity resonances. In this work, we theoretically show that this limitation can be overcome by engineering a momentum chirp in a BEC wavepacket. By balancing this chirp against the dynamical mean-field energy shift of the cavity during transmission, we predict enhanced resonant spectra and bistability features due to interaction-assisted tunneling that would be otherwise inaccessible. We show that this physics is readily observable with quasi-one-dimensional BECs of cold atoms colliding with a pair of light-induced Gaussian potential barriers forming the cavity. We also benchmark the requisite optimum chirp needed and characterize the contrast of near-discontinuous FP transmission spectra at an interacting resonance. Our findings enable the realization of technologies like matter-wave switching protocols, and high-precision velocity measurements; estimates of achievable sensitivity for the latter are provided.
summary: This theoretical work demonstrates how to overcome the limitation of mean-field interactions washing out nonlinear features in matter-wave interferometry. By applying a precisely engineered momentum anti-chirp to a Bose-Einstein condensate, the authors predict the realization of matter-wave bistability and high-contrast resonance spectra. This opens pathways for new quantum technologies like matter-wave switching and high-precision velocity sensing.
main_problem: The primary challenge is observing nonlinear matter-wave features, such as bistability, in interferometry experiments using Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) because mean-field interactions typically broaden and wash out these resonances.
main_result: The authors theoretically show that engineering a momentum anti-chirp in the BEC wavepacket can counteract the interaction-induced resonance shifts, thereby enabling the observation of enhanced resonant spectra and bistability features.
method: The analysis uses the 1D Gross-Pitaevskii equation (GPE) framework, modeling the system dynamics by coupling the incident matter wave to the quasi-bound states of the cavity barriers.
model_or_system: The system is a quasi-one-dimensional BEC interacting with a matter-wave Fabry-Perot (FP) cavity formed by light-induced Gaussian potential barriers. The dynamics are governed by the mean-field GPE, incorporating repulsive interatomic interactions ($g|\psi|^2\psi$).
key_observables: Transmission spectrum ($T$) as a function of incident wavepacket velocity ($v_0$), and the observation of bistability features.
important_parameters: The required optimum momentum chirp (anti-chirp) needed to balance the interaction-induced energy shift.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximating the initial state as Gaussian and employing various time-dependent approximations (e.g., assuming the source term is slowly varying) to solve the coupled differential equations.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the setup (BEC through a double-barrier FP), comparing non-interacting vs. interacting spectra, and showing the mechanism involving the anti-chirped wavepacket.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the physical limitation (interaction-induced broadening) to proposing the anti-chirp solution. It then develops the theoretical framework by modeling the time evolution of the coupling amplitudes and deriving the final transmission probability integral.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the practical limitations of using BECs for high-precision quantum measurements by providing a specific, controllable technique (momentum chirping) to counteract mean-field decoherence effects.
